narrative:
The model estimated a 73.8% chance that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. Because that is a high failure risk, your application was denied; this is not a judgment that you cannot succeed, but the prediction was treated as too serious to admit you. Your gender and race were not used in this prediction.

The strongest factor was your third-year grade decile: you were in decile 1, while accepted students averaged around 5.8, and this low standing pushed the prediction toward failure more than any other feature. Your first-year decile was the second most influential factor; it was also 1, versus an accepted average near 6, and it similarly increased the failure risk. Your undergraduate GPA was the third most important factor. At 3.80, it was above the accepted-student average of about 3.23, so it pushed toward passing, but it was not enough to offset the two grade-decile signals.

To move forward, ask for a human review of your file and explain any context behind the early grade standings; consider coursework or credentials that demonstrate current readiness, and discuss with admissions whether a conditional admission, interview, or additional academic work could be considered. A stronger recent record or other evidence of readiness may help change the decision.
